body:
I did some testing and I cannot reproduce your error in a very weird way:

I have one project, in which this error is always there, regardless of whether I enable SDFGI in the world environment or not.
I also tested whether it might react to the SSAO setting, but that didn't affect it either.

I have another project, in which the error is missing. And here again... No matter if I enable SDFGI/SSAO or not, the error won't appear.

I also tried adding/removing CSG objects with materials, but that didn't change anything either.
In one project I have the error, in the other I don't :(
Most likely this is caused by a corrupted shader cache. My guess is it will go away and not come back if you delete the cached shaders.

I did some tests with Godot 4.4.1 and in rare cases for some reason one of the shader cache files is wrongly created, more specifically the `0f1bcf11b9f7757773a7866f1cd2e297cb2acf5f.vulkan.cache` file in `%AppData%\Roaming\Godot\app_userdata\3D Environment Lighting Example\shader_cache\SceneForwardClusteredShaderRD\3adfc73c25d174aec0d3b2ecfc3241e77f9e51c8133f3048060810b80219419a`. 

In a normal situation this file has around 330KB, but in some cases this file is created with 0KB or 32KB. In the 0KB case the error raised is 

```
_load_from_cache: Condition "header != String(shader_file_header)" is true. Returning: false
  <C++ Source>  servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shader_rd.cpp:454 @ _load_from_cache()
```

And with the 32KB file is the same error as OP. I didn't found a realiable way to reproduce as seems to be random (maybe some race condition?). Deleting the project directory in `app_userdata` fixes the issue as mentioned by clayjohn.

I did some testing based on your comment.

I couldn't find the specific shader cache file you mentioned. The folder SceneForwardClusteredShaderRD is there but there is no subfolder named `3adfc...` and none of the 4 subfolders that were there contain a file with that name either. I imagine these names are randomly generated so that's not evidence of anything.

I did find a file with 331KB in size. This was the closest to the 330KB you mentioned. I believe these files are dependent on my combination of graphics card, driver, OS, etc so that's also not much evidence of anything.

My project right now started to show what  @Drako mentioned. The SDFGI option no longer has any effect on if the error appears or not, it always appears when I run the project. I then started flipping other options in WorldEnvironment and, this time, it is the SSR option that causes a change in behavior. Turning it on (which is what is set in the project I linked) makes the error appear, turning it off makes it go away.

Then I created a backup of the `%AppData%\Roaming\Godot\app_userdata\3D Environment Lighting Example` folder and ran the project again. This fixed the error, no matter what I set in the WorldEnvironment, the error no longer appears when I run the project.

Finally, I restored the old cache folder and ran the project and the error was back. I compared the two folders and there are a lot more files in the folder that produces the error, but I imagine this is due to me creating the project and attempting several configurations before reaching the one that I linked compared to the new folder where the project was already at a pre-defined state.

I don't know if that helps but should I attach my shader cache folder that produces the error?
